Hi Theo — attaching our completed questionnaire and a compact activation matrix. Below are the concise answers to the key technical points your security team flagged. If you want expanded runbook excerpts we included a PDF excerpt and the last full test report for your review.

High-level RTO/RPO commitments (per service tier)
- Hosted REST/text generation (stateless requests): RTO target = 120 seconds (warm fallback routing + warmed pools), RPO = 0 (requests are served directly; no queued state to recover).
- Long-running streaming sessions (session affinity): RTO target = 10–15 minutes to restore session continuity via proxy-based reconnect and prefix/KV cache warmup; RPO = best-effort (we do not replicate per-client ephemeral token streams across regions), therefore client reconnect logic is recommended.
- Embeddings/Batch jobs (durable ops): RTO = 15 minutes for failover to dedicated capacity in another region where pre-warmed workers exist; RPO <= 5 minutes for durable job metadata when using our recommended persistent storage backing (S3/Azure Blob).

Activation sequencing (short summary — full matrix attached)
1) Detection & triage (0–2 minutes): automated health checks escalate to on-call and trigger the routing policy.
2) Fallback routing (2–3 minutes): smart router shifts traffic to pre-warmed fallback model variants in the same region or cheaper cross-region pools depending on policy.
3) Region activation (3–15 minutes): if cross-region failover required, control plane promotes standby capacity in target region (pre-provisioned warm pools) and updates routing.
4) Session re-acquisition (5–20 minutes): clients reconnect; KV/prefix caching warmed progressively.
5) Post-failover validation (15–60 minutes): synthetic probes validate latency, token throughput, and model correctness; automated rollback available if regressions exceed thresholds.

Notes on data replication and audit trails
- Configuration/metadata: continuous replication of control-plane metadata (versions, routing policies) to our secondary region with strong consistency guarantees (multi-AZ within region + cross-region async replication).
- Runtime ephemeral caches: KV/prefix caches are optimized for latency and are not synchronously replicated cross-region; we treat them as warm-cache on failover with RPO = minutes. For customers requiring synchronous session state replication, we offer integration patterns (customer-managed external KV store) documented in the attached matrix.
- Logs & audit: all request/response logs and immutable audit trails are written to encrypted object storage in primary region and asynchronously replicated to secondary region; retention and replication configs are customer-configurable.

Testing cadence and evidence
- We recommend annual full-region failover tests plus quarterly tabletop exercises.
- Attached: dr_test_report_2026-11-02.pdf (redacted results), and dr_runbook_excerpt.pdf (operational playbook snippet).

Attachments: LumenBank_BCP_Qs_Filled.xlsx, regional_activation_matrix.csv, dr_runbook_excerpt.pdf, dr_test_report_2026-11-02.pdf, diagram_multiregion.svg
